svg.title: Writing ¿ ¡
svg.desc: 2 letters written one after another: ¿, ¡ (latin). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ¿: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class ¿: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>; ¡: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class ¡: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>. Source notes on variation: ¿: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of ¿, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 118 are two strokes; in 108 of those 118 the hook comes first and the dot last (in 10 the dot comes first). The hook starts at its top in 94 of the 118, sets off downward in 81, turns anticlockwise in 92 and ends at the lower right in 91. No school-model source for ¿ was found, so the order is the adult writers' majority. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the ¿ of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. ¡: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of ¡, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 119 are two strokes; in 114 of those 119 the bar comes first and the dot last, and 109 of the 119 draw the bar downward. No school-model source for ¡ was found, so the order is the adult writers' majority. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the ¡ of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
